newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market calmer at end of week.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market calmer at end of week.

text.p: Activity was subdued at the end of the week on London's sugar freight market with little firm business reported and no fresh inquiry, shipbrokers said on Friday.
CSR was close to fixing its recent order for 40,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Adabiya for July 15/20 and also for 20,000 tonnes to Savannah for mid-July, they said.
Booker fixed 6,700/7,300 tonnes from St Kitts to Nantes for July 7/12.

Jean Lion was said to have withdrawn its order for Santos to Algeria for prompt shipment, while Genoc was temporising on its enquiry for 6,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos to Tema, market sources said.
In other news, Syria re-tendered to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws for August shipment. The deadline for offers was set for July 15.
